fix.note: Often with negatives or 'why': 굳이 안 해도 돼요.

ex.en: You really don't have to come.

ex.s: 굳이 택시 탈 필요 없어요. 가까워요.
ex.en: There's no need to take a taxi. It's close.
Why did you go and buy the expensive one?

fix.en: to splash, spatter; to stand out

ex.en: Watch out, the oil splatters.
Water splashed when a car went by.
That outfit stands out too much.

ex.s: 이 서류 좀 부장님께 전달해 주세요.
ex.en: Please pass this document on to the manager.

ex.s: 엄마한테 제 말 좀 전달해 줘요.
ex.en: Please pass my message on to Mom.
The courier says he left it with the security office.

fix.note: More formal than 기차; used in announcements and on tickets.

ex.en: What time does the next train come?
The train left ten minutes late.
I booked a train to Busan.
Just go 100 meters from here.
I swam 500 meters at the pool today.

ex.s: 그 산은 높이가 천 미터쯤 돼요.
ex.en: That mountain is about a thousand meters high.

fix.note: Loanword; 색 and 색깔 are more everyday.

ex.en: I want to dye my hair this color.

ex.s: 컬러 프린트는 한 장에 이백 원이에요.
ex.en: Color prints are 200 won a page.
What's the trending color this year?
That singer debuted in 2015.
My friend's younger sibling debuted as an actor.

ex.s: 이 그룹은 데뷔한 지 십 년 됐어요.
ex.en: It's been ten years since this group debuted.

fix.note: Standard way Koreans describe home and shop sizes.

ex.en: How many pyeong is this apartment?

ex.s: 친구가 삼십 평 아파트로 이사 갔어요.
ex.en: My friend moved to a 30-pyeong apartment.

ex.s: 가게가 열 평 정도라서 좀 작아요.
ex.en: The shop is only about 10 pyeong, so it's a bit small.
In the evening we walked along the beach.
We booked a hotel near the beach.
If the weather's nice, let's go to the beach.
Prices are shown in English too.
An error message appeared on the screen.
Our hotel is marked on the map.

notes: Dropped 머물다 (dup of 머무르다 kv07-115), 제안하다/판단하다 (dup of nouns 제안/판단 in ev-13). Fixed a near-duplicate 굳이 example and awkward 좀 너무.
